## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `37837911e720f6c7cfa5bc284b3893b7373e057e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-field-readers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts (read on `origin/main` `aca58cdb6`, which holds #29387's merge `4138ce862`)

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: none moves. The diff is one file, `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md`, +2 lines, 0 deletions (`git diff origin/main...37837911e`). No `packages/spec/**`, no runtime, no changeset. Right.
- Public surface: none. The note documents what `origin/main` already does; it introduces no new behaviour and the runtime it describes landed as #29387. Right.
- Governed face: `docs/adr/**` is a Tier H register row, so this review is at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and the landing stays the maintainer's hand or a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` review. The PR is draft, auto-merge unarmed, head repo is the base repo. Right.
- Append-only: the diff adds a blank line and one blockquote paragraph after the 2026-10-28 note and before ⑨; the ⑧ bullet and both earlier notes are byte-unchanged. Right.
- Status line: untouched, which matches how the two earlier ⑧ notes landed (`c8cb510a5` 2026-10-26 and `9c1214006` 2026-10-28 each add 2 lines to this file and neither touches `**Status**`). The Status line's amendment entries record superseding decisions (ADR-0131, D4's api clause); a refinement note under ⑧ has never been one. Right.

### ② Semver level

No changeset, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Ruling-ref: 6573563853` on the body. A docs-only change publishes nothing, so no changeset is owed; the `patch` for `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` already shipped with #29387's `.changeset/29106-superuser-field-vote.md`. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: none raised on the PR. `open_questions`: none.
- The ruling's precondition (grep for a set declaring a super-user bit beside `readable: false` on the same object) was answered on the card before the runtime PR opened (issuecomment-6576959092, 0 declared sets) and re-swept in #29387's FAIL round 1 (two test fixtures, both edited there). Nothing left for this PR.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the implementation claim on the card (6576911116) names branch `claude/project-thread-q91xrq` and the card thread `session_01ADHkmSgjH5Vi4jT3KVJpvt`. This record is rendered by the seat session, not the thread that wrote the diff.
- Check-runs on `37837911e`: CHECKRUNS_PLACEHOLDER

### ④ Design judgment

The note is judged against the ruling of record 6573563853 (letter A) and the code on `origin/main` it cites.

- "`viewAllRecords` votes `readable: true`, and `modifyAllRecords` votes `readable: true` and `editable: true`. View All never grants an edit." Holds. `superuserFieldVote` returns `{ readable: true, editable: true }` the moment any set holds the `modify` bit and `{ readable: true, editable: false }` when only the `view` bit is held; `holdsSuperuserBypass(set, object, 'view')` is true for either bit (Modify All implies View All), `'modify'` for `modifyAllRecords` alone. The ruling binds "`viewAllRecords` votes `readable: true` … `modifyAllRecords` votes `editable: true`"; the note's "readable and editable" for Modify All is what shipped and is the only coherent reading (an editable field is readable). The vote only ever sets bits (`perm.readable = true; if (superVote.editable) perm.editable = true`), so View All neither grants nor removes an edit a declared entry gave. Right.
- "Who holds the bypass is the row-level answer: the set's own entry for the object if it has one, otherwise its `'*'` wildcard. One function answers it, `holdsSuperuserBypass`." Holds. `holdsSuperuserBypass` reads `objects[objectName] || objects['*']`; `PermissionEvaluator.superuserBypassSets` loops the sets through it and is what `hasSuperuserReadBypass` / `hasSuperuserWriteBypass` (the RLS and write bypass) read; `superuserFieldVote` loops the same function. The private posture is accepted by `superuserBypassSets` and does not change the answer (its doc says so and the body never reads `opts.isPrivate`), so the note's silence on posture is not a gap. Right.
- "`PermissionEvaluator.superuserBypassSets` reads it directly, and both field merges, `getFieldPermissions` and the row-blind `/auth/me/permissions` merge (`buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`), read it through `superuserFieldVote`." Holds, line for line: `permission-evaluator.ts` imports both from `@objectstack/core`, `getFieldPermissions` applies `superuserFieldVote(permissionSets, objectName)` after the declared-entry loop, and `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` applies it per object over the keys it holds; `current-user-endpoints.ts` calls `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions(resolved)` for the `fields` slot. Right.
- "So every reader of the merge answers the same: the list projection, record read, the sort and filter gate, the field-level write gate, `/auth/me/permissions` and `os explain`." Holds. The non-test callers of `getFieldPermissions` on `origin/main` are `security-plugin-field-readers.ts` (projections), `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts` (the input guard at the sort/filter gate, the write gate with `judge`, and `maskOperationResult`) and `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` (explain); `/auth/me/permissions` reads the other merge. No third merge exists. Right.
- "Before this, a set that granted the object through its super-user bits but declared no field entry cast no vote, so an app set's `readable: false` hid the field from a platform admin who also held the app set." This is the card's measured cause (#29106 body) and the doc comment on `superuserFieldVote` says the same. Right.
- "Union without deny is otherwise unchanged. A caller who holds no super-user set on the object is still narrowed by a declared mask, and a field's `requiredPermissions` capability gate still applies to everyone." Holds. The declared-entry loop is unchanged; `superuserFieldVote` returns `null` when no set holds a bit, and the merge is then exactly the pre-ruling merge. `foldFieldRequiredPermissions` is applied after `getFieldPermissions` in both the projection (`field-readers.ts`) and the mask (`object-inputs.ts`, "[ADR-0066 D3] AND-gate field-level requiredPermissions into the mask"), so the D3 AND-gate is outside the vote. Right.
- "One consequence: a set can no longer withhold a field from its own View All / Modify All holders. To withhold a field, grant the object without those bits." Right, and it is the consequence the runtime PR had to pay: both forced fixture edits in #29387 (`explain-principal-person.test.ts`, `resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts`) replaced a super-user bit with a row policy or `readScope`/`writeScope: 'org'` to keep a withheld field withheld. The note names the remedy that works. "Taking a field away from a super-user remains the job of the muting/deny layer ⑦ still owes" is the same sentence shape the 2026-10-26 note ends on and is consistent with precedence step 4 above.
- Shape and date convention: the note is a blockquote at the same two-space indent as the two earlier ⑧ notes, opens `**Note (2026-11-02) — <one-line summary> (#29106, ruling of record 6573563853, letter A).**`, which is the 2026-10-28 note's form (`(#26594, ruling of record 6457467702, letter B)`), and sits after the 2026-10-28 note in date order. The date is the ruling's date and the PR's open date. Right.
- Anchors (the adr-symbol-anchors grammar): the note writes one path-shaped code span, `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts`, a FILE-LEVEL anchor that resolves on `origin/main`; every symbol it names (`holdsSuperuserBypass`, `superuserFieldVote`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, `getFieldPermissions`, `superuserBypassSets`) is a bare code span, not a `path#symbol` anchor, and each exists in the file the prose attributes it to. No line anchor, no exemption marker. `/auth/me/permissions` is not path-shaped under the grammar. Resolves.
- First consumer and execution plan: the first consumer is the runtime that already landed (#29387, merge `4138ce862`, present under `origin/main` `aca58cdb6`, the base this branch restarted from), so the ADR records a decision whose implementation precedes it; nothing in the plan is left open.
- Should-fix, not must-fix: the note says the set "votes on **every** field of that object" while `superuserFieldVote` is applied only to fields the merge already holds an entry for (the doc comment: "an absent field is unrestricted anyway"). The two readings are observationally identical because ⑧'s own first sentence records that unlisted fields are visible and `computeForbiddenFieldWrites` forbids only declared locks, so the note's wording is the semantic truth and needs no change. Noted so a later reader does not look for an iteration over the object's field list.

**VERDICT: PASS**
